chunks: And from him, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād al-Nāb, from al-Ḥakam ibn al-Ḥakam, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying—and he was asked about salat (prayer) in churches and synagogues, so he said: “Pray in them; I have seen them—how clean they are.”
I said: Should one perform salat (prayer) in them even if they are praying in them? He said: “Yes. Do you not recite the Qur'an:
Say: Each acts according to his own manner, but your Lord knows best who is most guided in way.
Pray facing the qiblah, and place them to your west.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.الْبِيَعِ: churches or places of Christian worship
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, cited as proof in the ruling
key_terms.شَاكِلَتِهِ: one’s own manner or way of acting
key_terms.غَرِّبْهُمْ: place them to the west of yourself

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in churches and synagogues according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting salat (prayer) in churches and synagogues, emphasizing their cleanliness and instructing the worshipper to face the qiblah. The cited Qur'an verse is invoked to distinguish the Muslim’s act of worship from that of others, while maintaining proper orientation in prayer.
